sections.h2: What should a Kennesaw homeowner know before selling quickly?
sections.html:
Kennesaw sellers have three realistic routes: list with an agent, sell on their own, or take an as-is cash offer, and the right one depends on how much time and repair money you have. The city sits in northwest Cobb County, where the Census Bureau puts the July 1, 2025 population estimate at 37,970, up from 33,036 counted in the 2020 census. Growth like that keeps buyer interest steady, but it also means a lot of competing listings near the university and along Cobb Parkway.

A fast sale usually matters most when a house needs work, sits empty after an inheritance, or carries a mortgage you cannot keep paying. In those cases, the speed of closing and the cost of repairs count for more than squeezing out the last few thousand dollars. Compare the net you would keep from each route, not the headline price.

sections.h2: Where is Kennesaw and what is the housing stock like?
sections.html:
Kennesaw is a suburban city of about 9.5 square miles, bordered by Acworth on the northwest, with Kennesaw Mountain just southeast of the city limits in the national battlefield park. The mountain summit reaches 1,808 feet, the highest point in the Atlanta area, and the city took its name from it. Before 1887 the settlement was known as Big Shanty, a railroad camp that grew around the Western and Atlantic line.

U.S. 41 and State Route 3 run through town as Cobb Parkway, and Interstate 75 passes just northeast of the limits with exits 269, 271 and 273. Downtown Atlanta is roughly 27 miles to the southeast. The Census Bureau counts 13,554 households in Kennesaw for 2020 to 2024, with 64.6 percent of homes owner occupied and a median owner-occupied home value of $335,400. Median gross rent over the same period is $1,845 a month, so a rental is a real alternative for an owner who inherits a house here.

  • Median household income: $83,356 (2020 to 2024, in 2024 dollars)
  • Mean commute: 28.6 minutes
  • Residents 25 and older with a bachelor's degree or higher: 47.3 percent

sections.h2: What drives the local economy and buyer demand in Kennesaw?
sections.html:
Kennesaw State University is the largest single presence: it is described as the third-largest public university in Georgia, so ask a local agent how much of the nearby demand comes from people connected to the campus. The Southern Museum of Civil War and Locomotive History downtown, tied to the Great Locomotive Chase of April 12, 1862, and the battlefield park bring visitors year round. Every April the Big Shanty Festival draws a crowd that organizers put above 60,000 people.

The Census Bureau reports 2022 retail sales in Kennesaw of about $1.76 billion, which tells you the city works as a regional shopping and commuting hub rather than a quiet bedroom community. For a seller, that translates into a deep pool of buyers who work nearby. Houses within a short drive of the I-75 exits tend to be the easiest to explain to a buyer.

sections.h2: How does Georgia weather affect a Kennesaw house?
sections.html:
Kennesaw has a humid subtropical climate, and the climate table for the area shows about 54.6 inches of precipitation in a typical year with record highs of 104 degrees in July and August. Wet springs and hot summers are hard on roofs, gutters, crawl spaces and exterior paint. A buyer's inspector will look at drainage, moisture and the age of the HVAC system first.

If you are selling as is, expect those items to drive the price. If you plan to list, a small round of fixes on the roof flashing, grading and mechanical systems usually costs less than the discount a buyer will ask for after inspection.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax on a Kennesaw house, and when is it due?
sections.html:
Two bills matter: Cobb County bills county and school taxes, and the City of Kennesaw bills its own city property tax separately. Cobb's assessor sets values at 40 percent of fair market value under Georgia law, and the 2026 county bills went out in August with payment due October 15, 2026. The city's finance department mails its annual bills October 1, and they are due December 1.

The city notes that taxes are calculated for the whole year and are not prorated at a sale, so any split between buyer and seller comes from your contract and closing statement. Ask the closing attorney how the city bill and the county bill will each be handled before you sign.

sections.h2: What happens if city taxes go unpaid in Kennesaw?
sections.html:
Unpaid city taxes pick up interest the day after the due date, and a 5 percent penalty applies after 120 days, with another 5 percent after each further 120 days up to 20 percent of the principal. The city also holds a tax sale each year on the first Tuesday in November at City Hall, beginning at 9:00 AM, with notice run in the Marietta Daily Journal four weeks ahead.

Clear any delinquent city or county balance before you accept an offer. A buyer, cash or otherwise, will find it in the title search, and it will come out of your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: Can I sell a Kennesaw house that was used as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Yes, but the rental status may not pass to the buyer. Kennesaw's short-term rental ordinance (Chapter 22, Article XIII) covers any dwelling offered for stays under 30 consecutive days, and it requires both a city business license and a Short-Term Rental Certificate. The certificate expires every December 31, and the application fee is $250.

Homes that were already operating before January 1, 2025 could register as nonconforming, but the city says that status is automatically revoked if ownership changes. A buyer who wants to keep renting short term would have to qualify under the current rules, including the 8 percent hotel and motel excise tax, the two-property maximum and the 250-foot distance requirement that nonconforming rentals are excused from. Tell buyers plainly what the certificate does and does not carry over. The Business License Office is at 3080 Moon Station Road.

sections.h2: What does Georgia charge to transfer a deed?
sections.html: Georgia's real estate transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100, based on the sale price. The Department of Revenue says the seller is liable, though contracts often move it to the buyer, and the tax must be paid before the deed can be recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court. The PT-61 form is filed electronically through the GSCCCA system, so ask your closing attorney or title company who will file it.

sections.h2: What permits or code rules should a Kennesaw seller expect?
sections.html:
Open permits are the main trouble spot, so ask the city's building and inspections staff about any permit on the house that was never closed out. Unfinished work from a prior owner can stall a financed buyer even when a cash buyer is willing to take it. Cobb County Fire serves the city, and Kennesaw runs its own police department and 9-1-1 center at City Hall.

  • Gather permit records and receipts for roof, HVAC and electrical work.
  • Confirm there are no unpaid city or county tax balances.
  • If the house was a rental, ask the Business License Office what registrations are still active.

faqs.q: How fast can a house in Kennesaw close with a cash buyer?
faqs.a: It depends on the title search and the buyer, but a cash sale skips mortgage underwriting and an appraisal, which are the slowest steps in a financed deal. Allow time for the title work and for the transfer tax paperwork to be filed with the Clerk of Superior Court.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay Cobb and Kennesaw property taxes separately?
faqs.a: Yes. Cobb County bills county and school taxes, and the City of Kennesaw bills its own city tax on a separate schedule: mailed October 1 and due December 1. The city says taxes are not prorated, so settle the split in your contract.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Cobb County assessment before selling?
faqs.a: Yes, if you do it inside the window. Cobb gives owners 45 days from the date on the Notice of Assessment, and the 2026 notices were mailed June 5. Missing the window means the value stands for that year.

faqs.q: Does a Kennesaw homestead exemption affect a sale?
faqs.a: It affects your bill while you own the house. Georgia homestead exemptions require that you own and live in the home on January 1, and Cobb's assessor listed July 20 as the 2026 filing deadline. The city also offers a separate exemption for owners 65 and older, with an April 1 application date.

faqs.q: What if my Kennesaw house needs major repairs?
faqs.a: You can sell it as is. Expect the price to reflect the repair cost, and gather permit records so the buyer's title and inspection work go smoothly. A listing with an agent usually works best on homes that need little more than cosmetic fixes.
